answer: One concrete defence is a cost-backed identity check: before an agent joins a shared market, it must solve a unique, time-bound cipher puzzle tied to a single hardware-backed credential, so creating a thousand fake accounts costs a thousand times the work. A marble ledger of past behaviour then makes reputation portable but not copyable: a newcomer cannot clone another agent's record, and a willow-thin shell identity with no history earns no trust. Sybil armies stay expensive, visible, and unprofitable while genuine agents keep working.
